I have farmed this small shamba since I was a girl, and I learned everything from watching my mother and my neighbors. This plot is barely a piece of land — not even one hectare — so one full bag of fertilizer is too big and too expensive for me, and I do not have cash to waste. I will spread cow manure that I have collected from my animals, like I always do, and I will plant the seed I saved from last season mixed with beans. I will work this plot myself with my grandchildren, about twenty days over the whole season, and I will not hire anyone because I have no extra money for wages.
